sections.title: Format
sections.summary: Defines the key list that starts each spec section and the rules for how PRD sections count as covered.

requirements.text: Each spec section starts with a list of keys, before any prose.
IDs in keys are written in backticks and separated by commas.
A key applies to its section and every section below it.
A PRD section is covered when it, or a section under it, appears in some Implements, Defers or Context key.
A Defers or Context key also covers the sections under the one it names.
"Under" means in the heading tree, not by ID prefix; the top heading does not namespace its children.

decisions.text: Leave out @pierre/words.
decisions.why: It renders markdown to HTML strings through WebAssembly for streaming model output, the viewer would need innerHTML for it, and it knows nothing of {#id} headings; it may suit streaming session logs later.

decisions.text: Use @pierre/highlights for fenced code and diffs; leave out Shiki for code blocks.
decisions.why: Synchronous tokens become Foldkit spans without innerHTML; @pierre/diffs uses preferredHighlighter: highlights, sharing the same lexers.

decisions.text: Leave out a SQLite driver such as better-sqlite3.
decisions.why: @effect/sql-sqlite-node runs on node:sqlite, which needs no native build.

decisions.text: Leave out Rete, JointJS, Cytoscape, Drawflow and LiteGraph.
decisions.why: Each owns its scene and graph state, which would put state in two places beside the Foldkit model.

decisions.text: Leave out elkjs for layout; @dagrejs/dagre (MIT) is the choice when layout stops being fixed.
decisions.why: elkjs is EPL-2.0 or GPL-3.0 and 8 MB.

decisions.text: Leave out the AI SDK (ai, @ai-sdk/anthropic, @ai-sdk/typesafe-ai).
decisions.why: It adds a second schema language and a Promise API beside Effect; effect/ai covers both kinds of model.

decisions.text: Leave out Cloudflare AI Gateway as a dependency.
decisions.why: It is a proxy, not a library; baseUrl in config lets a user route through it.

decisions.text: Leave out Workers AI.
decisions.why: Cairn runs on the user's machine, not in a Worker.

decisions.text: Leave out an ORM such as Drizzle or Prisma.
decisions.why: One table needs no query builder, an ORM would declare row types a second time beside Effect Schema, and the same SqlClient runs on a Durable Object or D1 if v2 needs it.

sections.title: Links
sections.summary: Defines a Cairn deep link in `packages/contract/src/link.ts`. A link is a list of typed steps (section, passage, task, stack, segment, diff, commit, file, lines, turn, note) and its text is a URL path. One Effect Schema, `LinkFromPath`, decodes a path into steps and encodes steps back into a path, enforces the ordering rules and reports `LinkError`s.

requirements.text: `link.ts` must define both the Link (a list of steps) and its text form as a URL path. The step schemas and the one Schema that converts between path and steps must be the only definition of a link.
The viewer's route must read links through the link Schema, and `cairn link` must write them through it, so that a printed link and a copied link are always the same text.
`link.ts` must import IDs from `ids.ts` and `trailers.ts` and must never import from `index.ts`.
`index.ts` must re-export `link.ts`.
A Quote must be 1 to 500 characters long, with runs of whitespace collapsed to one space, and trimmed.
A NoteId must match `^n_[a-z0-9]{6,}$`.
In a `lines` step, `start` and `end` must be positive integers with start <= end.
A `file` step's path must be a non-empty string relative to the repo root.

Each step must be written as path segments: `/section/<id>`, `/passage/<id>/<quote>`, `/task/<id>`, `/stack/<root>`, `/segment/<root>`, `/diff/<head>`, `/commit/<sha>`, `/file/<path>`, `/lines/n<start>[-<end>]` or `/lines/o<start>[-<end>]` (`n` for new, `o` for old), `/turn/<session>/<turn>` and `/note/<id>`.
Every step argument must be encoded with `encodeURIComponent`, so a `/` in a file path becomes `%2F`.
The link with no steps must be written as `/`.
A trailing `/` must be accepted when a link is read and must never be written.
A single-line range must be written as `n40`, never as `n40-40`.
No step name may be `api`, `presence` or `assets`.
A `diff` step must come directly after a `task` step.
A `file` step must come directly after a `diff` or a `commit` step.
A `lines` step must come directly after a `file` step.
After the first `diff`, `commit` or `turn` step, only `file`, `lines` and `turn` steps may follow.
A link must have at most one `diff` or `commit` step and at most one `turn` step, and a `turn` step must be last.
A `note` step must be last.
Decoding must enforce the well-formedness rules for step order and count.
`LinkFromPath` must be an Effect Schema from the path string to `Link`, where decoding reads a link and encoding writes one.
Every ID in a link must decode through its own contract schema.

A decoding failure must be a `LinkError` giving the step's index, the step's name and the field path, e.g. `step 3 (file): must follow a diff or a commit` or `step 2 (diff).head: expected 40 lowercase hex characters`.
The contract package must take `fast-check` as a dev dependency, at the version that `spec.testing.model-based` pins.

tests.text: For every well-formed Link, generated from the step schemas with arbitraries that follow the ordering rules, encoding and then decoding gives the same steps, and encoding gives the same path each time.
Quotes and file paths that contain `/`, `%`, spaces, emoji and surrogate pairs come back unchanged after encoding and decoding.
The path for `cairn link prd.code-view t74 --file packages/cli/src/api.ts --line 40` is `/section/prd.code-view/task/t74/diff/<sha>/file/packages%2Fcli%2Fsrc%2Fapi.ts/lines/n40`.
A `file` step with no diff before it is refused, with an error that names the step and the field.
A `lines` step that does not follow a `file` step is refused, with an error that names the step and the field.
A `task` step after a `commit` step is refused, with an error that names the step and the field.
`/lines/n42-40` is refused, with an error that names the step and the field.
A bad SHA is refused, with an error that names the step and the field.
A bad percent-encoding is refused, with an error that names the step and the field.

sections.title: Stack order
sections.summary: stackOf orders drafts by dependency and returns a set of stacks: parentOf puts a task on the latest of its dependencies when they share one chain, and starts it from baseBranch after they land when they do not.

requirements.text: stackOf(feature, drafts, gates) returns the tasks as a set of stacks.
Tasks are topologically sorted by dependency; among tasks whose dependencies are placed, gated ones go first, then planner order.
IDs are t1… in that order, and branches are <feature>/<NN>-<slug>.
dependsOn is the draft's dependencies, as task IDs.
A task with no dependencies has parent null and starts a stack on baseBranch.
A task whose dependencies all lie on one chain takes the latest of them as its parent.
A task whose dependencies lie on different stacks has parent null and starts from baseBranch once every dependency has landed.
A cycle fails with a PlannerError naming the tasks in it.
worktreesOf gives each task the worktree of its parent or a dependency when that worktree's latest task is one it depends on and no other task has taken it next; otherwise a new one.
The first worktree is the repo's own checkout (null); the rest are wt-1, wt-2, ….
Tasks that can run at the same time never share a worktree.

The spec draws this repo's stacks as a Mermaid diagram from manifest.json: stacks numbered in the order of their first task and named for the second part of that task's first spec section, a solid arrow for a parent, a dashed arrow for any other dependency.
The diagram is redrawn whenever the manifest changes; a viewer test fails when the two disagree.
stackOf takes the manifest's existing tasks, returns them as they are, and orders drafts after them with IDs continuing from the highest.

sections.title: `cairn link`
sections.summary: Builds the `cairn link` CLI command. It turns its arguments, in the order given, into viewer link steps and prints the encoded path, by default with the `cairn serve` origin. It checks sections, tasks, commits and roots before printing. The section also sets the rule that agents and the orchestrator name places with `cairn link`.

requirements.text: `cairn link` prints a link into the viewer. It builds the steps from its arguments in the order they are given and writes the path with `LinkFromPath`, so its output is the path the viewer copies.
`stepsOfArgs(tokens, plan)` in `link-args.ts` reads the arguments left to right and is pure.
A token starting with `prd.` or `spec.` becomes a `section` step.
`--passage <text>` right after a section token turns that step into a `passage` step, with the text collapsed the way a quote is.
A token that is a task ID in the manifest becomes a `task` step.
`--commit <sha>` becomes a `commit` step.
`--file <path>` becomes a `file` step. When it follows a `task`, it first adds a `diff` step at the task's newest commit, read with `Git.log`.
`--line <n>` or `--line <n>-<m>` becomes a `lines` step on the new side. `--old` before it puts the step on the old side.
`--stack <root>`, `--segment <root>`, `--turn <session>/<turn>` and `--note <id>` each become their own step.
The command declares every option to `effect/cli`, so `--help` lists each option and `effect/cli` validates its value.
The command takes the order of its steps from the raw tokens after `link`, not from `effect/cli`'s parsed result.
Before printing, the command checks that each section ID is a heading in `prd.md` or `spec.md`.
Before printing, the command checks that each task is in the manifest.
Before printing, the command checks that a commit is known to git and, when it follows a task, carries that task's `Cairn-Task` trailer.
Before printing, the command checks that a stack or segment root has `parent: null`.
Before printing, the command checks that a task followed by `--file` has commits.
Before printing, the command checks that the steps are well formed.
A failed check exits with code 1 and a message naming the token, such as `unknown section prd.code-veiw`, `t74 has no commits, so it has no diff yet` or `--line must follow --file`.
The command does not check that a passage, a file or a line is still there. The viewer reports any that are missing.
The printed link is `http://localhost:4310` (the port `cairn serve` uses) followed by the path.
`--base <url>` sets another origin for the printed link. `--base ""` prints the path alone.
The command reads files and git and never writes.

`AGENTS.md` says that a pull request description, a gate notice and a board post name the place they are about with `cairn link`, and gives the `cairn link prd.code-view t74 --file packages/cli/src/api.ts --line 40` example.
The `detail` of a `blocked_on_human` event emitted by the orchestrator ends with `cairn link <task>`.
A pull request opened by `gt submit` links its task and the task's first PRD section.
Once there is a message board adapter, board posts name the place they are about with `cairn link`.

requirements.text: The model holds the trace, the screen, the reader's state, the hovered node, the detail panel's trail, the search, the presence state and the patches and sessions loaded so far.
`chainOf(trace, node)` is pure and returns the PRD sections, spec sections and tasks linked to a node, in both directions.

A 200 is decoded through the Trace schema and sends SettledLoadTrace with the trace; a 304 sends nothing.
A network or decode error sends SettledLoadTrace with the error, and the view shows the error above the last good trace.
The demo build (vite build --mode demo) loads demo-trace.json once and never polls.
A click does not pin a chain: a click on a task opens its detail, and the one thing a reader pins is a PRD section.

sections.title: Design system
sections.summary: Specifies the viewer's design tokens for a light and a dark palette, its three stylesheets, the classes and controls every view is built from, and the move of the code view to them.

requirements.text: Three stylesheets in `apps/viewer/src/ui/` are imported by `entry.ts` in order: `tokens.css` holds only custom properties on `:root`, `base.css` the page, the focus ring, prose and reduced motion, and `components.css` one class per piece.
Use Tailwind, CSS-in-JS or a preprocessor; a view applies a class with `h.Class` and keeps `h.Style` for a value that is computed.
The stylesheets select on the state attributes a view already sets, such as `aria-pressed`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-checked`, `aria-current`, `data-current` and `data-ran`.

Every colour is a token written once as `light-dark(<light>, <dark>)`; `:root` sets `color-scheme: light dark` and `index.html` a `color-scheme` meta tag, so the palette follows the system's setting with no switch, Model field or Message.
The palette is the section's table: the mockup's light values, with `--muted` one step darker and `--blocked-ink` added, and a dark value for each.
`--edge` and `--tint` are `color-mix()` of `--ink`, and text on any fill is `--ink`.

`light-only` sets `color-scheme: light` and the element's own colour and background again; highlighted code blocks, drawn diagrams and, until the canvas is removed, the canvas screen's `main` carry it.
Borders are `--line` (1.5px); radii are `--r-s` 4px, `--r-m` 8px and `--r-l` 12px; shadows are `--lift` and `--lift-l`, flat ink; a pressed button moves down 2px and loses its shadow.
Use a blurred shadow or a gradient.
The interface is `--mono` and prose is `--prose`, with no web font; sizes come from the eight `--t-*` tokens.
Motion uses `--ease` with `--d-fade` 150ms, `--d-press` 160ms and `--d-move` 240ms, animates only opacity, transform and colours, and is turned off under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
Every button, link and divider shows `:focus-visible` as a 2px `--ink` outline, 2px off the element.
`components.css` has the classes of the section's table of pieces, and the views it names use them and write no rule of their own for them.
`marks.ts` exports `dotView`, `tagView`, `gateView` and `labelView`.

`switchView` is `Switch.view` from `@foldkit/ui` drawn as a `btn`, with `role="switch"` and `aria-checked`; `disclosureView` is `Disclosure.view`, giving `aria-expanded` and, while open, `aria-controls`, with the panel rendered only while open.
`segmentedView` is a labelled `role="group"` of native buttons with `aria-pressed`; it does not use `@foldkit/ui`'s `RadioGroup`.

The code view, the tree, the diff style control, search, the search mark, code blocks and diagrams move to the classes and lose their inline colours; the canvas's own views keep theirs until they are deleted.

requirements.text: The reader is a top bar over three panes, the PRD, the spec and the stacks; the window does not scroll and each pane has its own vertical scroll.
`Screen` gains `Reader`; until the canvas is removed the viewer opens on the canvas and "Plan" and "Canvas" buttons move between the two.

`sectionAtTop(tops, line)` is the last section whose top is at or above the line, or the first when none is; the level 1 heading is never current.

Under each PRD heading a status line button shows the status word, the spec count and done/total tasks, and pins or unpins its section; a section with status deferred, context or unmapped shows a coverage note instead.

sections.title: Fuzzy matching
sections.summary: Index and rank fuzzy matches for titles, IDs and branches.

requirements.text: Build a pure search index from the loaded Trace: one entry per PRD section, spec section or task, retaining its existing Node identity. Index section titles and IDs and task titles and branch names; no server endpoint, persisted index or new contract field is needed.

Trim the query and match case-insensitively. Support ordered subsequences for abbreviations and a single insertion, deletion, substitution or adjacent transposition for query tokens of at least four characters; shorter tokens require exact, prefix or subsequence matches. Every whitespace-separated query token must match within one indexed field. Rank exact field matches first, then prefixes, contiguous matches, typo matches and subsequences; within a match class prefer titles, then IDs, then branches, then prose. Break remaining ties by score, source order and stable node key.

Return one result per node with its best matching field, score and sorted, non-overlapping, half-open UTF-16 ranges in the original visible text. Case normalization must preserve a mapping back to source positions and never split a surrogate pair. An empty query returns no search results. The same trace and query always produce the same order.

Cache the index by searchable trace content and rebuild it only when that content changes. Query changes reuse the index; status-only refreshes do not trigger markdown parsing. Keep matching and result derivation pure and use installed Effect core APIs. No search dependency is selected or added by this plan.

tests.text: Results have unique node identities, deterministic order and valid non-overlapping source ranges; normalized matches never split surrogate pairs.
Exact titles outrank fuzzy titles; abbreviations and one-edit typos match; blank and unmatched queries, punctuation and mixed-case Unicode are covered.

sections.title: Search controls and chain highlighting
sections.summary: Add search navigation and temporary chain highlighting.

requirements.text: Add window-local query and active-result state to the Schema-defined Model, with fact-named messages for query edits, result navigation, result selection and clearing. The pure update function derives results and reconciles the active node after trace refresh: retain it if still matched, otherwise choose the first result or none. Query edits reset to the first result; empty and unmatched queries have no active chain.

Render a labelled toolbar search input, result count and ranked result list showing kind, title and matched field. Use accessible combobox/listbox semantics with an active descendant, ArrowUp/ArrowDown navigation bounded at the list ends, Enter to select, pointer selection, and Escape to clear. Handle these keys only in the search control; they must not reach the reader's own keys, such as Escape. Announce the count and no-results state without stealing focus.

Selecting a result brings it into view in the reader. For a PRD section, the PRD pane scrolls to its heading. For a spec section or a task, the first PRD section of its chain, in document order, is the current section for as long as the result is active, ahead of the pin and without changing the pin or the PRD pane's scroll; its card, row and chip scroll into view in their own panes, and a result in a spec section's prose shows that card open while it is active. A spec section that implements no PRD section has no card to go to: selecting it opens it in the detail panel, the one case where a result opens the panel. Keep keyboard focus in search. Preview its chain as a hover does. Only the active result contributes a search chain; never union separate result chains into a synthetic chain.

Mark direct text matches with semantic mark nodes and a separate node outline, in PRD headings and prose, spec card headers, summaries and full sections, task rows and chips; related chain members get chain highlighting but no text marks unless they independently match. Hover remains the top preview, above search. Draw a curve as part of a chain only when both endpoints belong to that same chain. Use text labels or outlines as well as colour to identify the active result.

Clearing search removes its marks, outline, results and temporary chain while preserving the pinned section, the detail panel, document content and task state. The current section goes back to the pin or to the section at the top. A no-results query shows a message without dimming the panes. Pinning a section and opening a task continue to work. Keep the existing markdown lazy boundaries effective when queries change.

tests.text: Type an abbreviation or typo, navigate with arrows, select with Enter and pointer, and assert matching text, active result and connected-chain highlighting.
Search, hover and a pinned section coexist; clearing and Escape preserve the pin and the detail panel; zero matches leave the panes usable; refreshed and removed results reconcile correctly.

Select a spec section and a task whose PRD section is not the pinned one: its PRD section is current while the result is active and the pin comes back when the search is cleared; unrelated curves stay unlit. Select spec.format, which implements no PRD section, and find it open in the detail panel.

sections.title: Prose search and inline highlights
sections.summary: Search markdown prose with snippets and inline match highlights.

requirements.text: Extend the index to visible PRD and spec prose, owned by the nearest preceding section heading until the next heading of any level; nested sections own their text and do not duplicate it in their parent. Extract paragraphs, list items, table cells, link labels and inline code from the markdown AST. Exclude HTML/comments, heading ID attributes, link destinations, code fences and Mermaid content; diffs and session logs remain out of scope.

Keep a visible-text-to-AST-text-node offset map for each searchable prose block. Match within a paragraph, list paragraph or table cell, including across emphasis, links and inline code, but not across block or section boundaries. Reuse the fuzzy ranking and source ranges from fuzzy-matching; prose ranks below titles within a match class. Return one result per node, with its best match and a bounded context snippet from the matching block.

Render match ranges as semantic mark nodes in snippets and in document text leaves, splitting ranges across existing inline elements while preserving formatting, safe links, text selection and heading IDs. Do not rewrite source markdown, inject HTML or wrap DOM after rendering. Highlight the best matching field or prose block per result consistently with its snippet. For typo matches, mark the matched source word; for subsequences, mark matched characters.

Parse each changed document once and share its AST and position mapping between indexing and rendering. Query edits only rematch and render marks. Reconcile results and offsets when source content changes. Selecting a prose result brings the matched block into view, falling back to the owning section until block measurement is available; keep code highlighting and diagram mounts stable.

tests.text: Highlighting preserves the original visible text and every range maps to text in its owning section.
Find prose spanning bold text and a link, inspect the highlighted snippet and inline marks, select the matching block, and clear without losing formatting or pins.
Nested sections, inline code, tables, escaped markdown and Unicode retain correct offsets; comments, code fences and diagram labels do not match; query changes reuse the parsed AST.

sections.title: Curves
sections.summary: Specifies the curves that join the three panes for the current section: pure links and paths from measured rectangles, held inside their panes, measured by one Mount and lit along a chain on hover.

requirements.text: Curves are drawn for the current section only: one from its heading to each of its spec cards' headers, and one from each task row, a stray's too, to that task's chip.
`linksOf(cards)` is pure and returns those pairs as keys; each element a curve can end on carries its key in `data-wire`.
`wiresOf(links, boxes, panes)` is pure and returns, for each link with both ends measured, a Wire with its two keys, its path and `isOffPane`.
A curve runs from the middle of its source's right edge to the middle of its target's left edge; the PRD end leaves from the right edge of the PRD pane, level with the heading.
Each end's height is held inside its own pane, 8px in; a spec, row or chip end that had to be moved makes its curve `isOffPane`, and the PRD end does not count.
The path is a cubic bezier whose control points sit level with its ends, max(20, half the horizontal distance) in from each, computed by the reader itself.

A Mount on the reader body measures every `[data-wire]` element and the three panes at most once per animation frame, sends `MeasuredWires` only when a rectangle changed, and measures on mount, on a scroll in any pane, on a window resize, when a ResizeObserver on a pane or its content fires, and when `data-wires` changes.
`wiresView` is one fixed SVG over the reader body with no pointer events and `aria-hidden`; an `isOffPane` wire is dashed and fainter.
The PRD body and each card are lazy views, so a measurement renders the SVG again and nothing else.

A card's header, a task row and a chip send `HoveredNode` on pointer enter and focus and `LeftNode` on leave and blur; the hovered node's chain is drawn in ink and thicker, and every card, row and chip outside it is dimmed.

sections.title: Stacks
sections.summary: Lays the stacks pane out like the spec's stack diagram: one numbered box per stack, a chip per task bottom to top inside it, and the boxes in rows over the base branch by what they wait on, with the current section's tasks standing out.

requirements.text: `stacksOf(tasks)` is pure, replaces `stackLayoutOf`, and returns the stacks in number order, each with its number, root, area, level and cells.
A root is a task whose parent is null, names no task or would close a cycle; every other task belongs to its parent's stack, so each task is in exactly one stack.
Stacks are numbered from 1 in TaskIdOrder of their roots and labelled `Stack N · area`, the area being the second segment of the root's first spec section ID, or `Stack N` when it has none.
A task's row in its box is its depth along parent links, so a chain has no gaps; columns in a box follow the first-child-continues rule and are numbered by the ID of their first task.

A stack's level is 1 when it waits on no other stack, otherwise one more than the highest level among the stacks it waits on; a dependency that names no task or closes a cycle between stacks is ignored.

The view draws every stack whatever the current section is: the levels bottom to top, each a row of its stacks in number order aligned to the bottom, over a bar labelled with the base branch that is sticky at the bottom of the pane and is not a node; the pane starts scrolled to the bottom.
A stack is a box with `data-stack`, its number in a corner, `labelOf(stack)` as its title and aria-label, and a CSS grid of its cells, only as tall as its deepest chain.

A task is a chip: a button with `data-task` and `data-wire`, a status dot and the ID, a title and aria-label with the ID, title, branch, worktree and status, and a `--blocked` border when gated; it sends `ClickedTask`.
A chip in the current section's chain has `data-current`, an ink border and a hard shadow, and so does its box; every other chip is at 45% opacity and still takes focus, hover and clicks.
Over the diagram, sticky at the top: "N of M stacks hold this section · X of Y tasks done" and a legend.
Draw curves inside the pane: a chip sits on its parent, and the detail panel names a task's other dependencies.

sections.title: Resolving a link
sections.summary: Builds the pure `resolveLink` function that walks a deep link's steps against the trace and loaded data. It returns the steps that open, the first step still waiting for data, and what is missing. The section also builds `passageOf` for finding passages and `trunkOf` for finished trunks, plus the `linkNoticeView` status notice that tells the reader how far a link opened.

requirements.text: `resolveLink(trace, link, loaded)` in `links.ts` is pure.
The `loaded` argument of `resolveLink` holds the patches and sessions the model has received.
`resolveLink` checks the link's steps in order and returns `resolved`, `waiting` and `missing`.
`resolved` lists the steps that open, each with what it needs to open. A passage step comes with its mark ranges and a diff step comes with its route path.
`waiting` is the index of the first step whose data is not loaded yet, or none.
`missing` lists what did not resolve. At most one miss stops resolution, and passage misses do not stop it.
A miss has the shape `{ index, step, reason, message }`.
A section step resolves when a section in `trace.prd` or `trace.spec` has its ID. Otherwise it misses with `section-missing`, meaning the section was deleted.

A passage step resolves when its section resolves and the quote is found in that section. Otherwise it misses with `passage-changed`, which does not stop resolution, and the step opens as its section.
A task step resolves when `trace.tasks` has the task. Otherwise it misses with `task-missing`.
A stack step resolves when `stacksOf(trace.tasks)` has a stack with that root. Otherwise it misses with `stack-missing`.
A segment step resolves when that stack's finished trunk holds two or more tasks. Otherwise it misses with `segment-missing`.
A diff step resolves when its `head` is one of the preceding task's commits. Otherwise it misses with `commit-not-on-task`, meaning the branch was restacked or rewritten after the link was copied.
A commit step resolves when a task in the trace has the commit and, when a task precedes the step, that task is the preceding one. Otherwise it misses with `commit-missing` or `commit-not-on-task`.

A file step resolves when the patch of the diff or commit before it is loaded and has the path. Otherwise it misses with `patch-unavailable`, carrying the fetch error or the demo's missing patch, or with `file-not-in-diff`.
A lines step resolves when the file's hunks show every line from `start` to `end` on that side. Otherwise it misses with `lines-not-in-diff`.

A turn step resolves when a commit in the trace has the session, the session is loaded, and the session has a turn with that ID. Otherwise it misses with `session-missing`, with `sessions-unavailable` in the demo, or with `turn-missing`.
A note step never resolves yet. It misses with `notes-unavailable` because notes are not stored yet.
When a step's patch or session is not in `loaded`, `waiting` becomes that step's index and resolution stops there until the data arrives.
`trunkOf(stack, tasks)` in `links.ts` defines the finished trunk. It starts at the root and takes the run of `done` or `landed` tasks up to the first fork or the first unfinished task.
Resolution turns a patch into file names and hunk line ranges with the same patch-to-files step the diff view uses.
Resolution must not parse a patch any other way than the diff view's patch-to-files step.

`passageOf(index, section, quote)` finds a passage in the prose blocks its section owns. It takes the blocks and their visible-text offset maps from the prose index, where nested sections own their own text.
When finding a passage, the blocks' visible texts are joined with one space and each run of whitespace is collapsed to one space.
The first exact, case-sensitive match of the quote counts as the passage.
The passage match is mapped back to a range in each block it covers.
An edit anywhere else in the document leaves a passage's ranges pointing at the same text. An edit inside the passage removes the match.
`linkNoticeView` sits under the top bar of the reader and of the code view, with `role="status"`.
The link notice says how far the link opened and what is missing, for example: "Opened as far as task t74. `packages/cli/src/api.ts` is not in that diff."
A passage miss in the notice reads: "The passage changed: "…first 80 characters…" is no longer in Viewer."

sections.title: Opening a link
sections.summary: Makes the viewer a Foldkit application that owns the URL: it defines the viewer's only route, `linkRoute`, and `linkOf(model)`, which gives the canonical link of what is on screen. It also defines `openLink`, which applies a link step by step and fetches missing patches and sessions, and `withAddress`, which writes one browser history entry per step so Back walks the trail.

requirements.text: The viewer must become a Foldkit application that owns the URL.
`route.ts` must define `linkRoute` over `LinkFromPath` as the viewer's only route.
The implementer must read Foldkit's route and navigation declarations before writing `linkRoute`.

If Foldkit's route combinators can express a list of steps that print and parse from one definition, `linkRoute` must be built from them, with each argument's schema taken from the contract. Otherwise `linkRoute` must be one wildcard path run through `LinkFromPath`, and that Schema stays the single definition.
URL changes must arrive in the viewer as the `ChangedUrl` message.
`pushUrl` and `replaceUrl` must be commands.
A link must not carry a host, so that it opens the same way under `pnpm dev`, under `cairn serve` and on the demo site.
`pnpm dev` (Vite), `cairn serve` (through its `GET /*`) and the demo site must each answer any path that is not a file with the viewer's page.

The model must gain `reader.maybePassage` (the open passage's section and quote), `reader.maybeFocus` (a `stack` or `segment` and its root), `maybeLines` on the `Code` screen, `maybeHead` on `WholeTask`, `maybeLinkNotice`, and `maybePendingLink` (a link waiting for the first trace or for its data).
When `maybeHead` on `WholeTask` is None, the code view must show the task's newest commit, as before.

`linkOf(model)` in `links.ts` must be pure and must give the canonical link of what was opened, in this order: the pinned PRD section or a PRD passage in its place; a spec passage; the focused stack or segment; the detail trail's steps, each a `section` for a spec section or a `task`; a `task` step for the code view's task when that task is not the trail's last step; a `diff` with the head it shows, or a `commit`; the selected file, then `lines`; the highlighted turn.
A link must not hold the section at the top of the PRD pane, pane widths, the models switch, card density, cards opened by their header, or the search. Each viewer keeps those.
`openLink(model, link)` must resolve the link and clear what a link holds: the pin, the passage, the focus, the trail and the code view selection.
`openLink` must then apply each resolved step the way the click it stands for does.
A PRD section step must pin that section.
A spec section step must start the detail trail on the section, or add it to the trail when the panel is open.
A PRD passage step must pin the passage's section and mark the passage.

A spec passage step must pin the first PRD section the spec section implements when the pinned section is not one it implements. It must then open the spec section's card in `opened` and mark the passage.
A spec passage in a spec section that implements no PRD section must open in the detail panel, as search does.
A task step must start or extend the detail trail.
A stack or segment step must set the focus. The focused box gets `data-linked` and an ink outline, and for a segment its trunk's chips get them too.
A diff step must open the code view on the trail's last task at `head`.
A commit step must open the code view on that commit. When the trail's last task is a different one, the commit's task is first added to the trail.
A file step must select the file in the code view.
A lines step must set `maybeLines`.
A turn step must open the code view on the session's newest commit when no code step came before it, then highlight the turn as `ClickedTurn` does.
Passage marks must be `mark[data-link-passage]` nodes, placed by the same range splitting that search marks use.
Passage marks must have an ink underline and no fill, so a search mark inside one still shows.
The diff mount must gain a `data-lines` attribute, such as `n40-42`. Its `MutationObserver` reads the attribute to scroll to those lines and select them.
Line selection must use `@pierre/diffs`' line selection if `CodeView`'s declarations have one. Otherwise it must draw a line annotation, as the turn marks do.

For each step past the longest prefix the old link and the new link share, `openLink` must return a scroll command that brings the step into view, whether it is a heading, a passage's first mark, a card, a chip or a box.

For each patch or session the steps need that is not loaded, `openLink` must return a fetch command through the requests the code view already makes, so a link opened in a new window loads its diff and its turn.

When `ReceivedPatch` or `ReceivedSession` arrives for `maybePendingLink`, the link must be resolved again. A step that is now missing is taken out of the state, its notice is shown, and the address is replaced with `replaceUrl(linkOf(model))`.
A path that fails `LinkFromPath` decoding with a `LinkError`, or a step that `resolveLink` cannot find in the trace, must show the link notice.
`withAddress(update)` must wrap the viewer's update.

On first load, `init` must decode the URL into `maybePendingLink`, and the first trace must open it. History is then rewritten with one entry per step: `replaceUrl` with the first step, then `pushUrl` for each longer prefix.
A `ChangedUrl` from Back, Forward or a typed address must open that link without writing history.
A `ChangedUrl` whose link equals `linkOf(model)` must do nothing, which also absorbs the echo of the viewer's own `pushUrl`.

After any other message, if `linkOf` changed, the new link must be pushed. Each of these becomes one history entry, so Back undoes them one step at a time: pinning, opening a task or a spec section, cutting or shortening the trail, Escape, opening the code view, selecting in its tree, selecting lines, highlighting a turn, and "Back to the plan".
Escape with the detail panel closed must also clear the focus, as it unpins.

sections.title: Copying a link
sections.summary: Adds copy-link buttons across the viewer (PRD headings, spec cards, passages, the detail trail, stack boxes, the code view, diff lines and session turns). The buttons copy the same deep link the address bar holds, or a shorter link that opens one step on its own. The section also defines the pure `aloneOf` function in `links.ts`, which builds that shortest link.

requirements.text: Copying the address bar must copy the deep link. The copy-link buttons must give the same link text without navigating to it.
`aloneOf(link, index)` in `links.ts` must be pure. It must return the shortest link that opens the given step by itself.
For `aloneOf`, a section, passage, task, stack, segment, commit, turn or note step must be its own step, so the link holds only that step.
For `aloneOf`, a diff step alone must be its task plus the diff.
For `aloneOf`, a file step alone must be the diff or commit before it plus the file. For a diff, the diff's task comes first.
For `aloneOf`, a lines step alone must be the steps that the file needs, then the file, then the lines.
`copyLinkView({ path, label }, h)` must render a small `btn`. Clicking it must send `ClickedCopyLink` with the path.
On `ClickedCopyLink`, the update must run a Command that writes `location.origin` plus the path to the clipboard and then sends `CompletedCopyLink`.
After `CompletedCopyLink`, the copy-link button must read "copied" until the next render, as the section ID button does.
A PRD heading must have a "Copy link" button beside its section ID button that copies `/section/<id>` alone.
The pinned PRD section's status line row must copy the link up to that section's step.
A spec card header must have a "Copy link" button that copies the section alone.
The `TrackSelection` subscription in `subscription/selection.ts` must listen to `selectionchange` and handle it at most once per animation frame.
When both ends of the selection lie in one `[data-passage]` element, `TrackSelection` must send `SelectedPassage` with the section and the quote.
A PRD section's prose wrapper must carry its section ID in `data-passage`. A spec card's full section body must too.
The passage quote must be the selection's text, trimmed, with whitespace collapsed.
When the selection leaves a `[data-passage]` element, `TrackSelection` must send `ClearedPassageSelection`.

While a passage is selected, the section's status line row (in the PRD) or the card header (in the spec) must show "Copy link to passage". Clicking it opens the passage as a step, which pins the section and marks the passage, and copies the link up to that step.
When the selected passage is over 500 characters, the "Copy link to passage" button must be disabled, with the title "Select at most 500 characters to link to them."
In the detail panel, each step of the trail must have a "Copy link" button that copies the path up to that step.
The detail panel's heading must copy its task or spec section alone.
In the stacks pane, each box must have a "Copy link" button in its corner that copies `/stack/<root>`.
A stack box whose finished trunk holds two or more tasks must also have "Copy link to finished trunk", which copies `/segment/<root>`.
The code view top bar must have "Copy link", which copies the whole path.
The code view top bar must have "Copy alone", which copies `aloneOf` its last step. That step is the lines when lines are selected, and otherwise the file, the diff or the commit.

The diff mount must turn a line selection into `SelectedDiffLines` with the side, start and end. It uses the line selection callback of `@pierre/diffs`, or a click listener on the line-number gutter if the library has no such callback.
A line selection must join the current link.
In the session pane, an opened turn must have "Copy link", which copies the path up to that turn.
A link to lines copied from a task's diff must carry the `diff` step's head: the commit the code view showed when the link was copied. The link then opens on the same code after more commits land.
